opportunities.title: Spoofed Transfers, Not Stolen Keys: Why the Bitget $352M Hack Should Scare You More Than a Private-Key Leak
opportunities.why_now: Bitget's CEO just confirmed the $352M breach came from spoofed transfers on backend systems, not compromised keys — a scarier failure mode than the usual narrative.
opportunities.angle: Technical breakdown of the attack vector vs. the 'cold wallet is safe' myth, ending on what this means for exchange trust assumptions

opportunities.title: KelpDAO Just Sued LayerZero for 'Endorsing' the Setup That Got It Hacked for $292M — Audits Are About to Get a Lot Scarier
opportunities.why_now: This is the first major lawsuit alleging a bridge provider's endorsement of an architecture created legal liability for the $292M exploit.
opportunities.angle: Explainer on the precedent this sets for infra providers, auditors, and 'we reviewed this' language in DeFi

opportunities.title: AI Can Doxx Your 'Anonymous' Wallet Now — Here's What That Actually Means for Your OpSec
opportunities.why_now: Fresh reporting on AI-powered deanonymization tools directly threatens the pseudonymity crypto users assume they have.
opportunities.angle: Practical opsec checklist framed around what AI deanonymization can and can't do today, written for people who think they're already careful

opportunities.title: The £10K Reward Won't Fix This: Crypto's Wrench-Attack Problem Is a Security Model Failure, Not Bad Luck
opportunities.why_now: A UK couple was just attacked in their home over crypto holdings, the latest in a rising pattern of physical extraction attacks tied to on-chain visibility.
opportunities.angle: Argue that on-chain transparency + public wealth signaling is the real vulnerability, with concrete steps to reduce physical exposure

opportunities.title: 3,832 NFTs in 'Protective Custody': What a Whitehat Rescue Looks Like When It Actually Works
opportunities.why_now: Magic Eden's incident is a rare case where a vulnerability was caught and contained before becoming a headline nine-figure loss.
opportunities.angle: Contrast this clean whitehat intervention against the same week's Bitget disaster to illustrate what 'good' incident response looks like
